title: api: request/response schema versioning — deprecations, beta headers, backward-compat shims
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce explicit API schema versioning and beta header for opt-in access to new structured-output and function-calling schema. Adds non-breaking backward-compat shims for common client patterns. Advise clients to opt into the new behavior via Accept-Api-Version or X-Redwood-Beta headers. No SLA impact.
description:
Motivation: We've been iterating on structured output, streaming chunk semantics, and function-calling ergonomics. To stabilize rolling changes and avoid accidental regressions for customers, this PR introduces a lightweight API request/response schema versioning system, an opt-in beta header, and server-side backward-compat shims for common older client patterns.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds Accept-Api-Version and X-Redwood-Beta headers to allow clients to opt into v2 schema and experimental behaviors. Introduces v2 response schema for structured_output (field rename structured_output_v2 -> structured_output), explicit function_call object (instead of the previous string-based heuristics), and clarified streaming chunk envelope (adds chunk_type and seq fields). Implements server-side shims to accept legacy forms: function_call as string "name(args)" and streaming chunks without chunk_type; server will normalize to v2 internally and emit deprecation warnings in response headers (X-Redwood-Warning). Provides a feature-flag gated rollout (ENV: API_SCHEMA_VERSIONING=enabled) and a runtime toggle per-customer to gradually flip on v2 by default.

Highlights: - Non-breaking by default: clients that do not send Accept-Api-Version or X-Redwood-Beta continue to receive v1 behavior. - Opt-in beta: clients can send "Accept-Api-Version: v2" or "X-Redwood-Beta: structured-output-v2" to opt into new semantics. - Backward-compat shims: parse legacy function_call strings, accept older streaming chunks, and rewrite responses for older clients when necessary. - Deprecation headers: responses include X-Redwood-Warning when a legacy shim is applied, and metrics are emitted to track usage of legacy paths. - Tests: unit, integration, and e2e streaming tests added to catch regressions. - Docs: migration guide in redwood-docs (link: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-docs/pull/324) and changelog note.

Checklist:
- [x] Add Accept-Api-Version and X-Redwood-Beta header handling (server + proxy).
- [x] Implement v2 structured_output schema and canonical function_call object.
- [x] Add runtime shims for legacy function_call and streaming envelopes.
- [x] Emit deprecation warnings in response headers and metrics.
- [x] Add unit/integration/e2e tests for both v1 and v2 paths.
- [x] Update docs and migration guide.

Migration notes for clients (short): To opt in, set Accept-Api-Version: v2 and check responses for X-Redwood-Warning; update client parsing to expect structured_output as a JSON object with fields {type, content, annotations} and function_call as {name, arguments}. Streaming clients should handle "chunk_type" values: "stdout", "delta", "final" and fallback when absent. We will keep the shims for at least one quarter before turning on stricter validation (ENG-1302).

Related: Linear ENG-1298 (schema versioning rollout), ENG-1302 (migration telemetries), docs PR https://github.com/redwood/redwood-docs/pull/324, SDK updates forthcoming in redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript.

Security: No auth surface changes. Telemetry added is limited to schema-version header and shim usage flags (no request body capture).

Rollout plan: Feature-flag behind API_SCHEMA_VERSIONING. Start with internal + canary tenants, then opt-in beta customers, then gradual global opt-in over 2 weeks. Planned enforcement: soft deprecation warnings for 90 days, then stricter validation controlled by flag.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez (2026-02-19): Left a few nits around header parsing edge cases. Please ensure header matching is case-insensitive and supports multiple comma-delimited values. Also confirm we don't leak X-Redwood-Warning in internal-only responses.
Maya Chen (2026-02-19): Addressed header case-insensitivity and added unit tests. X-Redwood-Warning now gated by customer visibility flag. See updated unit tests.

merge_commit_summary: squash: api(schema-versioning): add beta header and backward compat shims for structured output and function calling — includes tests and docs
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: default behavior unchanged unless client opts in. We will monitor shim usage via metrics 'api.legacy_shim.usage' and deprecations via 'api.schema_deprecation.warnings'. Plan to remove shims after the 90-day soft deprecation window unless major customers are still on legacy paths.
